newsitem.title: EGYPT: SOCCER-AL AHLI OPT OUT OF AFRICAN CHAMPIONS' CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AL AHLI OPT OUT OF AFRICAN CHAMPIONS' CUP.

text.p: Four former winners head the list of entries for next year's African Champions' Cup but one of Africa's most successful clubs has surprisingly opted to sit it out.

Egyptian club Al Ahli, winner of six African club competition titles in the last 14 years, qualified for the draw after winning the Egyptian championship in May but have turned down the chance to play, African soccer officials said on Tuesday.
No official reason has been given but officials said the team were probably still "sore" after being suspended by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) two years ago for player violence.
Al Ahli were banned for a year after their defeat by Cairo rivals Zamalek in the African Super Cup in Johannesburg in January 1994 triggered fighting.

Ironically, Zamalek will take Al Ahli's place in the 1997 cup and will be among the early favourites, along with other former winners Mouloudia Alger of Algeria, Raja Casablanca of Morocco and Club Africain of Tunisia.
Mouloudia Alger will be chasing their first Champions' Cup title in 20 years. Raja Casablanca won in 1989 and Club Africain two years later.
Zamalek, seeking a record fourth triumph in the African Champions' Cup, play Shooting Stars of Nigeria in Cairo on Friday in the second leg of this year's final.
A total of 38 entries have been received but last-minute confirmation was still awaited from several countries, CAF said. Some 41 countries played in this year's competition.
The draw will be finalised on Tuesday but only released on Thursday to allow for possible adjustments.

The draws for African competitions are traditionally made by the confederation's committee to ensure geographical proximity in fixtures because of the financial constraints on most African clubs. In contrast, in Europe ties are determined by seedings and the drawing of lots.
Next year sees the introduction of the African Champions' League when the tournament reaches the quarter-final stage.
The eight teams will be divided into two groups of four. They will play on a league basis with the two group winners contesting the final at the end of the year.
